newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers stake in vegetable oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers stake in vegetable oil firm.

text.p: Egypt said on Sunday it was offering 350,000 shares of its stake in the partly privatised vegetable oil company Misr Gulf Oil Processing (MIGOP) to one or more anchor investors.

The state-owned Egyptian Development Industrial Bank said in a published advertisement that the offer for 173,000 shares in Egyptian pounds and 177,000 shares in dollars would be open from April 30 until May 8.
The minimum offer price will be the closing price of the company's shares on April 29, the day before the offer opens.

MIGOP shares are listed on the Cairo stock exchange in pounds and dollars. The stock closed on Thursday up two pounds at 52, while the dollar-denominated shares ended trading $0.5 dollars higher at $14.
Alamiya Brokerage and Okaz Financial Brokerage are the agents for the sale.
The advertisement said Egyptian Development Industrial Bank holds 8.38 percent of MIGOP's total shares.
Other shareholders in the joint stock company include Gulf Arab Investment Company, Islamic Development Bank-Jeddah, Suez Canal Bank and individual investors.

The advertisement said MIGOP's net distributable profit, yet to be allocated, for the 1996 financial year was 22.806 million pounds, up from 2.717 million pounds net distributable allocated profit in 1995.
The company's financial year begins on January 1 and ends on December 31.
The company has had a 10-year tax exemption on profits which ends at the end of the 1997 financial year, the advertisement said.
Unallocated net sales for 1996 were 331.745 million pounds compared to allocated net sales of 273.303 million in 1995.
